1.pericope_label: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD hath anointed me
debates: Who the speaker of the soliloquy is
Whether the clause means the opening of a prison or the opening of the eyes
Whether the second divine name belongs to the text
outliers: Clarke reports manuscript support for writing two words as one, giving not merely release from prison but every kind of liberty
Gill insists that what rested on the speaker was the person of the Spirit and not gifts only
themes: A soliloquy whose speaker is disputed
A prophecy with a near sense and a remote one
The year of jubilee taken as the figure of the work
Three offices gathered into one commission

2.pericope_label: To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God
debates: Whether the acceptable year is a year at all
Whether a word has dropped out of the text at the third verse
What the trees of righteousness are
outliers: Clarke follows a conjecture that supplies a lost word; Ellicott explains the same gap as the prophet correcting himself while writing
themes: A year of favour set against a single day
A word for liberty drawn from the flight of a bird
Mourning garments exchanged for festival ones
Righteousness figured as a tree that does not fade

4.pericope_label: They shall build the old wastes, and ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD
debates: Whether a word has dropped out of the fourth verse
How badly the seventh verse has been damaged
outliers: Ellicott parts company with commentators who make the strangers the builders
Clarke doubts that the desolations of many generations can refer to the exile at all
themes: Ruins repaired as the figure of a soul restored
A whole people raised to a priestly rank
Rough work assigned to others
Double given in place of shame

8.pericope_label: For I the LORD love judgment, and their seed shall be known among the Gentiles
debates: Whether the clause condemns robbery brought as an offering or robbery with violence
Whether the word means their work or their recompense
Whether the seed is known by increase or by holiness
outliers: Ellicott sets the received rendering aside as not fitting the context and follows the Septuagint and the Targum
Clarke expects converted Jews to remain visibly distinct long after they are known to be Christians
themes: A clause whose sense turns on the pointing alone
Righteousness demanded whole or not at all
A covenant renewed after it has been broken on one side
Recognition rather than fame

10.pericope_label: I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation
debates: Who sings the song of the tenth verse
What the ornament of the bridegroom is
Whether the second divine name at the last verse belongs to the text
outliers: Henry refuses to choose between the two speakers and takes the one as a type of the other
Clarke reports a judgement that the divine name is interpolated because it makes the line longer than those around it
themes: A song whose singer is disputed
Salvation and righteousness worn as clothing
A bridegroom dressed like a priest
Growth rather than triumph as the figure of the end
